argument: Scoped support, and it clears a lead rather than the whole chapter: the nine-section inventory and the lonely one-card Plants block are exactly what the owning chapters require, so neither is a structural defect. The chapter that owns tradition membership hands the arcane side an eight-discipline list, plants and mind included (10-magic-system:87), and states in the same passage that plants answers to both traditions, which is why a discipline can appear in both spell chapters at once (10:91). The divine chapter demonstrates the twin on the primal side with its own plant section and a plant card that requires a primal focus (12-divine-spells:368, 12:371). So the arcane Plants heading at 11:334 holding one card matches the pattern rather than signalling a deleted section, and the eight arcane section names reproduce the tradition list exactly. The file's other anatomy claims also hold under a mechanical sweep: fifteen cantrip cards and fifty-three leveled cards, which is the count the opener states (11:19), every one of the sixty-eight cards printing a Discipline header line and either a full weak/standard/strong outcome block (sixty-five cards) or a single effect line (the three ward cards, 11:643 through 11:657), with tier ranks ascending inside each section. What this clears is the section inventory and card-format completeness; the three per-card and placement defects I filed separately stand, and the ledger's existing cross-chapter items on repeated card text and armor wording are untouched by this.

evidence.claim: The tradition chapter's arcane list names eight disciplines, plants and mind among them, and the file's nine headings reproduce that set (10-magic-system:87).

evidence.claim: Mechanical sweep written and run over the source file: 68 card headings, 65 cards printing weak/standard/strong exactly once each, 3 ward cards printing a lone effect line, 0 cards missing a Discipline header line, 0 cards with a malformed outcome order, and heading levels of 9 sections plus 68 cards.
